records.what_adobe_says: Mostly a built-in model, with one real setup choice. A step in Workfront Fusion (the automation tool sold with Workfront) lets a team type a plain-English instruction and has an AI model carry it out in Workfront. Out of the box it runs on a Claude model that Adobe manages, capped at 25 dollars of use per organization per month. A team that wants more, or wants its own provider, can enter its own OpenAI or Anthropic (or Amazon Bedrock) key. That is a link to the client's own OpenAI or Anthropic account, not to the ChatGPT or Claude apps. Suggested handling: a prerequisite note on a Workfront automation service, not a new line on the canvas. Second reader: every fact the research states is on Adobe's page word for word, and the page carries no beta or preview label. It stays "partly confirmed" only because Adobe names OpenAI and Anthropic here as model providers reached with a key, and never names the ChatGPT or Claude apps.

verdicts_changed.why: The research presents this as an OpenAI and ChatGPT link. The one Adobe page that could be read names only the standards (ACP and UCP), never OpenAI or ChatGPT, and words it as a commitment, not as something available. A ChatGPT checkout would be a connection if it were real, so "not a connection" hid the real finding: the claim is not backed.

The first reader found no Adobe source and called it an older name for Coworker. An official press release (news.adobe.com, June 22, 2026) does name Adobe Marketing Agent, beside Coworker, as available on AI platforms from Anthropic and OpenAI. So the product and its availability are confirmed; the ChatGPT and Claude details are not.
